carnia.label: Carnia, Friuli
eras: Republic of Venice — Patria del Friuli
Parish registers only, kept by the parish and now largely with the diocese of Udine
Civil registration lapses; the parish register is the record again for these fifty years.

carniola.label: Carniola and the Slovene lands
eras: Catholic parish registers in Latin, kept by the parish, from the later sixteenth century where they survive.
From 1784 the registers become a state instrument in a fixed columnar form, with house numbers
French civil registration for four years, in the Napoleonic form, before the Habsburgs take it back.
Austria — the Duchy of Carniola and Lower Styria
Registers in Latin and German; the parish keeps the original and the diocese holds a copy, which is why a burned parish is not always a lost record.
Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes, then Yugoslavia
Partitioned between Germany, Italy and Hungary
Three occupiers, three filing systems, and the deportations of Slovene families from the German zone.
Yugoslavia — the Socialist Republic of Slovenia
Civil registration is taken from the church and given to the municipality in 1946
SIRAnet searches the finding aids of all six regional archives at once, which is the single most useful thing about Slovenian research.

dalmatia.label: Dalmatia
eras: Governed from Zadar, and its records went there.
A short Italian occupation with its own paperwork, easy to miss between two Yugoslav periods.

istria-central.label: Central Istria
eras: No parish registers exist anywhere for this period
The books stayed with the parish and were gathered to Pazin in the twentieth century
The parish books continue unbroken; the regime change is invisible in them.
Registration moves to the matični ured
Current registration is with the matični ured in Pazin

istria-south.label: Southern Istria
eras: Republic of Venice — Istria da Mar
Pula becomes the imperial navy's main port, and the population triples
The esodo: most of the Italian-speaking population leaves between 1945 and 1956

istria-west.label: Western Istria

lazio.label: Lazio (the Papal heartland)
eras: Rome and the surrounding Duchy of Rome became part of the Papal States in 756, after the Donation of Pepin.
Declared in February 1798 by General Berthier; Neapolitan troops ended it in October 1799.
Papal rule was formally restored in June 1800 after a French reoccupation.
Napoleon annexed the rest of the Papal States, including Rome, on 17 May 1809.
Restored by the Congress of Vienna
Italian forces captured Rome on 20 September 1870 and a plebiscite in October annexed it.

queensland.label: Queensland
eras: Immigration, naturalisation and wartime alien registration are FEDERAL and are at the National Archives in Canberra, not with the state

santafe.label: Santa Fe — Rosario
eras: Spanish Empire — Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata
Catholic parish registers only, in Spanish, kept by the parish and now largely with the diocese.
Independence changes the flag and not the filing: the parish register is still the only record of a birth.

Ottoman rule was restored in October 1813, until the Second Serbian Uprising of 1815.

transvaal.label: The Transvaal
eras: The Sand River Convention of 17 January 1852 recognised Boer independence north of the Vaal; the first president took office in 1857 and the 1858 constitution fixed the n
Annexed by Britain on 12 April 1877; the Pretoria Convention of 3 August 1881 restored self-government.
Under British suzerainty until the London Convention of 27 February 1884; British forces occupied the republic after the Second Boer War began on 11 October 1899.
The Treaty of Vereeniging of 31 May 1902 ended the republic; limited self-government came in 1906–07.
Union of South Africa — Province of the Transvaal

trentino.label: Trentino
eras: A state of the Holy Roman Empire from 1027; the Council of Trent met there in 1545–1563.
Principality of Trent, under the County of Tyrol
Secularised in 1803 and placed under the Habsburg County of Tyrol.
Bavaria annexed Trent together with Tyrol under the Peace of Pressburg.
Napoleonic Kingdom of Italy — Department of Alto Adige
Bavaria ceded southern Tyrol in the Treaty of Schönbrunn of 14 October 1809; the change took effect on 10 June 1810.
Back under the Austrian crown land of Tyrol until the First World War.
Italy occupied the area in 1918 and the 1919 Treaty of Saint-Germain-en-Laye formally ceded it.

veneto.label: The Veneto
eras: Venice took Treviso and Bassano del Grappa in 1339; the fall of the Carrara of Padua is dated 1406.
The Treaty of Campo Formio gave Venice to Austria on 17 October 1797.
Gained by the Treaty of Pressburg of 26 December 1805; Venetia's annexation was announced on 30 March 1806 and ratified on 1 May.
The kingdom was formally established on 9 June 1815
The Treaty of Vienna of 12 October 1866 ceded Venetia to France, which handed it to Italy on 19 October; a plebiscite on 21–22 October confirmed it.

vojna-krajina.label: The Military Frontier — Vojna krajina
eras: Habsburg military frontier, under Graz and Vienna
The frontier was carved out of Croatia and Slavonia and put under the war council, not the ban
THE TRAP, AND IT IS THE REASON THIS REGION EXISTS
The frontier was wound down over thirty years and abolished by degrees; the regimental series end at different dates in different districts, which is why a family can van
The frontier is incorporated into Croatia-Slavonia and its ground finally files like everywhere else: civil registration from 1895, county and parish series thereafter.
Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes; Yugoslavia
Parish registers continue; the state registers of 1895 onward are held by the registry offices and pass to the state archives after a century.
Records of these four years are scattered and incomplete, and much of the Orthodox parish record of this ground was destroyed with the communities that kept it.
Church registers were gathered into the state archives; civil registration is with the matični ured of each municipality.
ARHiNET is the catalogue of the Croatian state archives and is the place to establish what survives before writing.

influenza-1918: Influenza A (H1N1) pandemic that spread worldwide in several waves from spring 1918 to 1920, infecting about a third of humanity, with notably high mortality among young adults.
Estimates run from about 17 million (a 2018 reassessment) through at least 50 million (CDC) to figures above 100 million; about 500 million were infected. Covers 1918-192
covid-19: Global pandemic of the coronavirus SARS-CoV-2, first detected in Wuhan, China, in December 2019; WHO assessed it as a pandemic on 11 March 2020 and ended the health emergency in May 2023.

cholera-second: Cholera spread from India across Western Asia to Russia, Europe, Britain and the Americas, and east to China and Japan, reaching Britain in October 1831.
No overall total is given; the article describes hundreds of thousands of deaths in Europe, with local figures such as about 100,000 each in Russia and France and 6,536 i
trail-of-tears: The US government forcibly moved about 60,000 Cherokee, Muscogee, Seminole, Chickasaw and Choctaw people from the Southeast to Indian Territory after 1830, with many dying of exposure, disea
Wikipedia's infobox totals 13,200 to 16,700 deaths across the Cherokee (4,000), Creek and Seminole (3,000), Chickasaw (3,500) and Choctaw (2,500-6,000) removals.
jasenovac: Jasenovac concentration camp complex and Ustaša killings
Camps run by the Ustasa regime of the Independent State of Croatia, centred on the village of Jasenovac, held and killed Serbs, Roma, Jews and political opponents from August 1941 to April 1
Recent scholarship and the US Holocaust Memorial Museum put deaths in the Jasenovac camp complex at roughly 77,000 to 100,000 across 1941-45; the memorial's named list is
holocaust: The systematic murder of European Jews by Nazi Germany and its collaborators, carried out by mass shootings in eastern Europe and by gassing at extermination camps, mainly in occupied Poland
The Nazi German regime and its allies and collaborators murdered about six million Jews in 1941-45; the Wikipedia article gives 5.7 million as a conservative lower figure
dresden: British and American bombers struck Dresden in four raids from 13 to 15 February 1945, causing a firestorm that destroyed much of the city centre in the last months of the war in Europe.
A historians' commission set up by Dresden city council (report 2010) found that between 22,700 and 25,000 people died in the British and US raids of 13-15 February 1945.
